hana: hi team, day 1 head-scratcher. installed asdf and python 3.10 on my M1 mac. building wheels for a deps with `cryptography` fails: it can't find OpenSSL headers. i followed brew instructions but pip install still errors with "unable to find openssl/ssl.h". any mac/openssl/asdf tips?

liam: welcome! common issue is that asdf's python build uses the system headers unless you export flags for Homebrew openssl before compiling. what did you install? brew or system openssl? `brew --prefix openssl@3` will show path.

hana: brew shows `/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3`. i tried `export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib"` and `export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include"` then `asdf install python 3.10.12` but still get same error during pip wheel build.

sam: two things to check: 1) make sure you exported and exported before running the asdf build (the env must be present when `python-build` compiles). 2) ensure `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` includes openssl pkgconfig: `export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib/pkgconfig:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH"`. on Apple Silicon also set `export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"` so build finds brew's pkg-config.

liam: also good to run `brew reinstall openssl@3` then `brew link --force --overwrite openssl@3` is sometimes needed (brew warns about not linking by default). after that, re-run the asdf install with the envs in the same shell. Example full sequence we use in onboarding doc: 
```
export PATH="$(brew --prefix)/bin:$PATH"
export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib/pkgconfig:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH"
asdf install python 3.10.12
```

hana: ah i had the exports in ~/.zshrc but i restarted shell and then re-ran asdf install from a different terminal where those exports weren't set. will try again from same session. one more wrinkle: after i get install working, how do i make sure requests/urllib3 trusts our internal corp CA? dev servers with MITM proxy complaining about cert verify failures.

sam: for internal CA, easiest is to add the CA to the macOS keychain (so system curl/openssl see it) and for python's cert store (used by requests) you may need to update `certifi` or point the `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` env var to a file containing the internal CA. Example: `export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/redwood-corp.pem` or in your `.env` for local dev.

liam: note that if you compile python against brew openssl, the interpreter will use OpenSSL's cert store paths. some folks re-run `python -m pip install certifi` then `python -c "import certifi; print(certifi.where())"` and append the internal CA to that path or set `SSL_CERT_FILE` to a custom bundle. we keep a small helper in dotfiles: `scripts/update-cert-bundle` that concatenates certifi + local CA and exports SSL_CERT_FILE for dev shells.

hana: nice. what about zshrc vs zprofile? i put brew/asdf exports in .zshrc but mac GUI apps (like VS Code from Spotlight) didn't pick them up so my GUI terminals still used system python. which file should i use?

sam: for zsh on mac, put login-related PATH/env exports in `~/.zprofile` (loads for login shells and GUI-launched apps) and interactive extras in `~/.zshrc`. We recommend `~/.zprofile` contain minimal PATH and LDFLAGS/PKG_CONFIG exports so everything launched by launchd inherits them. Keep `source $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh` in `.zprofile` before other PATH changes.

liam: final practical steps: remove any brew python (`brew uninstall python` if you want rust-free), put the openssl envs + asdf init at top of `~/.zprofile`, run the brew link commands, then `asdf install` from that same shell. after success, run `python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel` then `pip install cryptography` to verify wheels build.

hana: did the full sequence (moved exports to .zprofile, added PKG_CONFIG_PATH, brew link) and reinstalled python via asdf. now `pip install cryptography` completes. added `export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=$HOME/.certs/redwood.pem` to .env for local dev and tests now pass. thanks!! :tada:

security-bot: Reminder: don't commit internal CA certs to public repos. Use the internal secure store or config management to distribute certs. See https://redwood.internal/security/tls for approved workflows.
